author_or_org: Suvodip Dey, Yi-Jyun Sun, Gokhan Tur, Dilek Hakkani-Tur

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Users tend to over-rely on LLM-based AI agents and accept AI suggestions even when the AI is wrong.
claims.quote: On the other hand, users tend to over-rely on LLM-based AI agents, accepting AI's suggestion even when it is wrong.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Positive friction such as explanations or user confirmations has been proposed as a mitigation for overreliance in AI-supported decision-making systems.
claims.quote: Adding positive friction, such as explanations or getting user confirmations, has been proposed as a mitigation in AI-supported decision-making systems.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The paper proposes an accountability model for LLM-based task-oriented dialogue agents that uses friction turns when the model is uncertain or makes errors associated with dialogue state tracking, in order to address user overreliance.
claims.quote: In this paper, we propose an accountability model for LLM-based task-oriented dialogue agents to address user overreliance via friction turns in cases of model uncertainty and errors associated with dialogue state tracking (DST).

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The accountability model augments an LLM with an additional accountability head that acts as a binary classifier to predict relevant dialogue-state slots mentioned in the conversation.
claims.quote: The accountability model is an augmented LLM with an additional accountability head that functions as a binary classifier to predict the relevant slots of the dialogue state mentioned in the conversation.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The proposed approach enables reliable estimation of AI agent errors and guides the decoder to generate more accurate actions.
claims.quote: Our empirical findings demonstrate that the proposed approach not only enables reliable estimation of AI agent errors but also guides the decoder in generating more accurate actions.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Incorporating accountability heads into modern LLMs improves joint goal accuracy of dialogue state tracking output by around 3% absolute.
claims.quote: We observe around 3% absolute improvement in joint goal accuracy (JGA) of DST output by incorporating accountability heads into modern LLMs.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Self-correcting detected errors increases JGA from 67.13 to 70.51, achieving state-of-the-art DST performance; error correction through user confirmations as a friction turn achieves a similar performance gain and may reduce user overreliance.
claims.quote: Self-correcting the detected errors further increases the JGA from 67.13 to 70.51, achieving state-of-the-art DST performance. Finally, we show that error correction through user confirmations (friction turn) achieves a similar performance gain, highlighting its potential to reduce user overreliance.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: LLMs are known to hallucinate and produce responses that seem plausible but are factually incorrect.
claims.quote: However, they are also well known to hallucinate, producing responses that seem plausible but are factually incorrect.
